descriptionChirho: The literal hand as a body part, including singular, dual, and plural forms with all pronominal suffixes and prepositions; the concrete limb used for grasping, striking, lifting, etc.

Metaphorical extension of hand to mean power, strength, dominion, or agency; often in construct phrases like 'the hand of the LORD' meaning God's power, or 'into the hand of' meaning into the power/control of.
Spatial sense meaning side, bank (of a river), or beside/alongside a location; Arabic جَانِب, Korean 곁/옆, Hindi किनारे, Swahili karibu na/kando ya.
A place, station, or memorial pillar/stele (cf. 2 Sam 18:18 Absalom's monument); Hindi स्थान (place), Korean 자리 (seat/place), Spanish lugar.
Projecting wooden pegs or tenons used to join tabernacle boards together (Exodus 26, 36); Hindi चूलें, Korean 촉들, Spanish espigas.
Handle of a vessel, axle of a stand, or armrest of a throne; a projecting part grasped or rested upon; Arabic مَقَابِض (handles), Hindi हत्थों (handles), Spanish brazos/asas.
Idiomatic prepositional usage (כְּיַד) meaning 'according to the ability, bounty, or generosity of'; used for proportional giving or royal provision.
